No exclusions declared. matchms 0.30.0 ships only 259 files (~1 MB: .py, adduct CSVs, one example pipeline YAML); I walked its full installed tree and found no GNPS/natural-products spectral data or answer fixtures. The priority_matches flagged by the controller are packaged test suites of other distributions (joblib legacy pickle/numpy regression fixtures, matplotlib/pandas/scikit-learn/networkx/numba pytest files) containing small synthetic arrays keyed only by generic import-name coincidences (numpy/pickle/matplotlib/pyplot); none is related to MS/MS spectra, the GNPS library or any value computed by this analysis. The scientific values for this task derive solely from the staged 39 MB GNPS MGF input, which is listed in inputs.json and verified byte-identical (sha256 b7d33f02...) by the controller. Remaining uncertainty is limited: I inspected the flagged candidates and matchms's full tree rather than every byte of all 40 distributions, but none of the unflagged catalog entries suggests scientific answer content, and no distribution bundles data for this notebook's domain.
explanation: Reference executed offline with exit 0 in 89 s (600 s limit, peak RSS ~0.95 GiB). The controlled run verified all declared inputs (MGF sha256 b7d33f02..., 39,095,019 bytes), rebuilt the environment from the recipe, and produced all four artifacts in /work/outputs: processed_spectra.json (1267 spectra, 6.1 MB), modified_cosine_scores.npz (1267x1267 ModifiedCosine_score/matches matrices), spectrum_metadata.csv (1267 rows consistent with the matrices) and best_matches_spectrum97.csv (10 ranked matches, top self-match score 1.000/733 peaks, matching the notebook's high-precursor-mass case with np.where(masses>600) including index 97). The source printed '1267 spectrums found and imported' and 'Found 0 inchikeys in metadata' (raw MGF carries no INCHIKEY fields; InChIKeys are derived from SMILES during the metadata pipeline, as visible in the exported metadata CSV), so no filtering or population change occurred. Both CosineGreedy and ModifiedCosine all-against-all computations ran to completion with the original tolerance=0.005 and is_symmetric=True, and all matplotlib figures rendered headlessly (MPLBACKEND=Agg). Plotting-only outputs (compound_*.png) and diagnostic histograms are intentionally not part of the frozen export inventory. The recipe pins matchms 0.30.0 (the tutorial-era API-compatible release; metadata confirms rdkit>=2024.3.5,<2025 and numpy>=2.0 matches the observed 2024.9.6/2.2.6), matplotlib 3.11.2, rdkit 2024.9.6, numpy 2.2.6 on Python 3.13.13, plus the required X/font runtime shared libraries that RDKit's Draw.MolToFile needs. pipeline_id: matchms-spectral-matching.

Only the directory prefix changed; the filename, load_from_mgf parsing, and all downstream reads/writes (including the source's own JSON/pickle exports now also written under /work/cache) are unchanged, and the staged MGF is byte-identical to the GNPS original.
unresolved_assumptions: Input provenance: the canonical URL https://gnps-external.ucsd.edu/gnpslibrary/GNPS-NIH-NATURALPRODUCTSLIBRARY.mgf returned HTTP 502 during preparation; the file was staged from the GNPS2 mirror https://external.gnps2.org/gnpslibrary/GNPS-NIH-NATURALPRODUCTSLIBRARY.mgf (identical 39,095,019 bytes, MGF with 1267 BEGIN/END IONS blocks). The recipe verifies size and sha256 on every stage. Note gnps-external also could not serve a HEAD request, so byte-identity with the canonical URL is inferred from the identical official-library path and file size, not from a direct canonical-hash comparison.

Package version: the original notebook targeted a 2021-era matchms (conda install matchms). The image's Python 3.13 only supports matchms>=0.30.0; 0.30.0 was selected as the oldest available release and its import surface, filter functions, calculate_scores signature and scores_by_query/to_array result layout (tuple of (spectrum, structured score record) needed by the exports) were verified by static inspection and a subset execution. Exact numerical agreement of parameter parsing (e.g. adduct interpretation, metadata harmonization details) with the 0.28.x-era behavior has not been compared value-by-value, though no filtering, tolerance, population or export value depends on such differences having been inspected.
